# ;dhanna; and its sisters

ta3leeq, ilghaa2: Peled <https://www.academia.edu/101820592/Amal_and_ibtid%C4%81_in_Medieval_Arabic_Grammatical_Tradition>

;wip_warn;

## Introduction

There are some verbs that,
in addition to a ;faa3il;,
also
generally require two ;mafulb;s.
;dhanna; is one of these verbs.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

There are other verbs similar to ;dhanna;.
We will study them collectively as ";dhanna; and its sisters."

## The ;isnaad; of the ;dhanna; sentence

The basic ;j_ism; consists of a ;mubtada; and a ;xabar;.
For example:

(@) [زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the ;mubtada;
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is its ;xabar;.
Both are in the ;ucase; because it is a basic ;j_ism;.
In terms of its ;isnaad;,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the ;musnadi;
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is the ;musnad;.
(Technically, the ;musnad; is [أَخ]{.ar}. And it in turn is a ;mudaf; to the ;mudafil; [كَ]{.ar}.
But loosely speaking, we can say that the ;musnad; is the bundled [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}.)
With the ;musnadi; and the ;musnad; in place, the sentence is ;isnaad_comp;.

Now consider the following sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
the verb ;dhanna;
takes the ;mubtada; and ;xabar; of example (),
and makes them into ;mafulb;s.
The verb ;dhanna;
requires a ;faa3il; (as usual),
which is the pronoun [تُ]{.ar} [I]{.trans}.
And it also requires two ;mafulb;s:
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the first ;mafulb;
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the second ;mafulb;.

This sentence is peculiar in its ;isnaad;.
This is because the ;3umdah; elements are the two ;mafulb;s.
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the ;musnadi;
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the ;musnad;.^[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3@ 433]
The sentence is only ;isnaad_comp; when both ;mafulb;s are in place.
Unlike normal ;j_f3l;s,
the verb ;dhanna; and its ;faa3il; are not the ;3umdah; elements of the sentence.
Rather ;dhanna; is the ;pregov;.
Figure () depicts the ;3amal; of example ().

DIAGRAM

If one or both of the ;mafulb;s are missing,
then the sentence is not (generally) sufficiently ;isnaad_comp;:

(@) ;x; [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}  
    [I thought Zayd]{.trans}  

(@) ;x; [ظَنَنْتُ]{.ar}  
    [I thought]{.trans}  

In examples () and () above, depending on context,
the listener may be left wondering,
"You thought Zayd to be what?"
and
"You thought what?",
respectively.
However, as we will see in the examples, sometimes, some of these verbs
that fall in ;dhanna; and its sisters
don't require two ;mafulb;s.
In which cases the sentence will be ;isnaad_comp; without them.

Parallels of the ;isnaad; of the ;dhanna; sentence
may be found in the ;kaana; and ;inna; sentences:

(@) [كَانَ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [Zayd was your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدٌ]{.ar}, the ;faa3il;/;ism_of;, is the ;musnadi;.
    [أَخَاكَ]{.ar}, the ;mafulb;/;xabar;, is the ;musnad;.
    ;kaana; is the ;pregov;.)


(@) [إِنَّ زَيْدًا أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
    [@peled_sentence_types@ 188]{.citex}  
    [Indeed Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدًا]{.ar}, the ;ism_of;, is the ;musnadi;.
    [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}, the ;xabar;, is the ;musnad;.
    ;inna; is the ;pregov;.)

Similar to (;naqis;) ;kaana; sentences,
the ;dhanna; sentence may be categorized as a ;j_f3l;.
And, like in the case of ;naqis; ;kaana;,
the verb and its ;faa3il; don't make the sentence ;isnaad_comp;.



## Categories of ;dhanna; and its sisters

There are many verbs that behave similar to ;dhanna;,
in that they require two ;mafulb;s.
These verbs may be sub-categorized into:

1. *#;af3aal_quloob;*. These verbs indicate that the ;faa3il; believes the first ;mafulb; to be something that is indicated by the second ;mafulb;.
   For example:
   [ظَنَّ]{.ar} [to think, conjecture]{.trans},
   [عَلِمَ]{.ar} [to know]{.trans},
   [حَسِبَ]{.ar} [to reckon]{.trans},
   [خَالَ]{.ar} [to imagine]{.trans},
   [زَعَمَ]{.ar} [to claim]{.trans},
   [رَأَىٰ]{.ar} [to opine]{.trans},
   and more.

2. *#;af3aal_tasyeer;*. These verbs indicate that the ;faa3il; changes or leaves the ;mafulb; in a state that is indicated by the second ;mafulb;.
   For example:
   [صَيَّرَ]{.ar} [to make (something) become]{.trans},
   [اتَّخَذَ]{.ar} [to take (something) for oneself]{.trans},
   [تَرَكَ]{.ar} [to leave (something)]{.trans},
   [جَعَلَ]{.ar} [to make (something)]{.trans},
   and more.

Some verbs, like [جَعَلَ]{.ar} can fall into both categories, where [جَعَلَ]{.ar} can also mean [to believe]{.trans}, in addition to [to make]{.trans}.

We will discuss these verbs individually in section\ () below.

## ;dhanna; and its sisters in passive voice

When ;dhanna; and its sisters are used in the passive voice,
the first ;mafulb;
(the one which is the ;mubtada; in the basic ;j_ism;)
is made the ;naib_faa3il; in the ;ucase;.
And the second ;mafulb;
(the one which is the ;xabar; in the basic ;j_ism;)
remains a ;mafulb; in the ;acase;.
So, example () above, becomes in the passive voice:

(@) [ظُنَّ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd was thought to be your brother.]{.trans}

Similarly,

(@) [زَيْدٌ مَظْنُونٌ شُجَاعًا]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/52D]{.citex}  
    [Zayd is thought to be brave.]{.trans}  

## Example sentences of ;dhanna; and its sisters

#### ;dhanna; {.unnumbered}

The basic meaning of ;dhanna; is to conjecture.
So, with this original meaning, it implies a lack of certainty.


However, in some contexts, it can imply something that is thought with certainty.

#### [عَلِمَ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

(@) [عَلِمْتُكَ الْبَاذِلَ الْمَعْرُوفَ]{.ar}
    [@wright@ 2/49B]{.citex}  
    [I have known you to be liberal in the exercise of bounty.]{.trans}  

(@) [فَإِنۡ **عَلِمۡتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤۡمِنَـٰتࣲ** فَلَا تَرۡجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِۖ]{.quran}
    [https://quran.com/60/10 cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/325]{.citex}  
    [And if **you know them to be believers**, then do not return them to the disbelievers;]{.trans}  

When [عَلِمَ]{.ar} has only the meaning
[to know (something)]{.trans}
and not
[to know (something) to be (something)]{.trans}
then it may take only one ;mafulb;.
For example:

(@) [وَٱللَّهُ أَخۡرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمۡ **لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ شَیۡـࣰٔا**]{.quran}
    [@https://quran.com/16/78@ cited by @nahw_arabi@ 1/236]{.citex}  
    [And Allāh has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers **not knowing a thing**]{.trans}  

(@) [لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ النَّظَائِرَ** الَّتِي كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهِنَّ سُورَتَيْنِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ]{.ar}
    [@https://sunnah.com/muslim:822e@]{.citex}  
    [**I know the manners** in which the Messenger of ;Allah; ;pbuh; recited two ;surah;s in one [rakeah]{.trn2}.]{.trans}
